Fire is not independent of fuel. Fuel is not dependent upon fire. Fuel is not independent of fire."},"philosophy":{"insight":"The chapter's pivot: four negations (catuṣkoṭi). Fire is NOT inherently dependent on fuel. NOT inherently independent of fuel. Same for fuel relative to fire. All four logical options under inherent existence are exhausted. This IS emptiness.","madhyamaka":"Not inherently dependent (vv.8-11 showed this fails). Not inherently independent (vv.1-7 showed this fails — fire needs fuel). The same applies symmetrically to fuel. Neither dependence nor independence characterizes their inherent relationship because they have NO inherent relationship — only conventional.","quantum":"A qubit before measurement is neither definitely 0 nor definitely 1. It transcends classical binary categories. Nāgārjuna's fire-fuel similarly transcends the dependent/independent binary — it's not that they're \"both\" or \"neither\" but that the categories don't apply inherently.","bridge":"Both quantum superposition and Mādhyamika's tetralemma transcend classical binaries. QM: not wave, not particle, not both, not neither (in the classical sense). Mādhyamika: not dependent, not independent, not both, not neither (inherently).","accessible":"Is the number zero positive or negative? Neither — it transcends the positive/negative binary. Fire-fuel similarly transcend the dependent/independent binary under inherent existence.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, fire depends on fuel — this is perfectly true. Ultimately, neither inherent dependence nor inherent independence applies. Both truths are needed for a complete understanding.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying fire and fuel have no relationship. Saying their relationship is conventional and empty, not captured by any inherent category (dependent, independent, both, or neither)."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Superposition and Transcending Classical Binaries","score":78,"strength":"High","explanation":"Quantum superposition: a system is neither definitely in state A nor definitely in state B — it transcends the classical binary. Not inherently independent (vv.1-7: independence leads to eternal fire, no connection, no burning). Both options fail under inherent existence. Conventionally, fire depends on fuel — and this is fine.","realLifeExample":"Is a river's bank dependent on the river, or independent? Neither inherently. The bank shapes the river and the river shapes the bank — conventionally interdependent, ultimately empty of inherent status."},{"q":"What is the catuṣkoṭi (tetralemma)?","a":"The four-cornered logic: (1) A, (2) not-A, (3) both A and not-A, (4) neither A nor not-A. Nāgārjuna negates all four under inherent existence. This is not nihilism but the exhaustion of ALL inherent categories — showing phenomena are empty of all inherent classification.","realLifeExample":"Is light a wave? No. A particle? No. Both? No (in the classical sense). Neither? No (it manifests as both in different contexts). Light transcends the categories."},{"q":"How does superposition relate?","a":"Before measurement, a qubit isn't 0 or 1 — it's in a superposition that transcends the classical binary. Similarly, fire-fuel aren't inherently dependent or independent — they exist in a conventional \"superposition\" of relationship that transcends inherent categories.","realLifeExample":"A coin spinning in the air is neither heads nor tails until it lands. The spinning state transcends the heads/tails binary."},{"q":"Why is this the Middle Way?","a":"Eternalism (inherent existence/independence) is one extreme. Nihilism (inherent non-existence) is another. The Middle Way negates BOTH without landing on either. V.12's four negations exemplify this: not dependent (avoiding one extreme), not independent (avoiding the other).","realLifeExample":"A tightrope walker doesn't lean left (eternalism) or right (nihilism). Balance is not a \"third position\" but the skill of not falling to either side."},{"q":"Does this mean fire-fuel have NO relationship?","a":"No! They have a CONVENTIONAL relationship: fire burns fuel, fuel supports fire. What v.12 negates is any INHERENT characterization of this relationship.
